analysis_notes.gap_analysis_summary: Torah #252 is a two-sentence aphorism that contains no bechina (parallel/shared-nature) language anywhere in its text. All relationships in the teaching are eitza (cause-and-effect): (1) אחדות בין הצדיקים (unity among tzaddikim) → צדקה לא מזיקה (charity causes no financial loss); (2) אחדות בין הצדיקים (unity among tzaddikim) → מסירת נפש לא מזיקה (self-sacrifice causes no physical death). The five concepts appearing in the text — אחדות (unity), צדיקים (tzaddikim), צדקה (charity), מסירת נפש (self-sacrifice), חיים (remaining alive) — are not equated as bechinat each other. They form a causal chain, not a thematic equivalence cluster. Therefore no additions to packages are warranted, and no dataset nodes are unassigned because the bechina subgraph for this Torah is empty.

concepts_in_text.role_in_text: cause (eitza) — the enabling condition for both outcomes
the action that normally causes financial loss, but does not under unity
the action that normally causes physical death, but does not under unity
the agents whose unity creates the enabling condition
the outcome — the person survives after mesiras nefesh
